key_insight: A tunable XXZ interaction combined with single-qubit operations provides a unified route to arbitrary two-qubit gates in neutral-atom processors.
engineering_relevance: Flexible native gate selection could reduce circuit depth and compilation overhead without requiring a separate interaction mechanism for each gate.
method: Propose a Rydberg-atom realization of XXZ coupling with tunable anisotropy.
Combine the interaction with optimally controlled global microwave pulses.
Target B, QFT, iSWAP, √iSWAP, and a continuous CZ-to-iSWAP gate family.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports implementations of these target gates but provides no numerical fidelities, noise benchmarks, or experimental validation.
watch_item: Experimental feasibility will depend on interaction tunability and pulse robustness under realistic neutral-atom noise.
paper_title: Unified architecture for arbitrary two-qubit gates with neutral atoms
